values.value: • Use the relationship as an accelerator, not as a substitute for qualification. • Leverage trust to get candid feedback on budget, competition, and decision path. • Bring up previous wins, responsiveness, or service quality as credibility anchors. • Ask for access to wider stakeholders while goodwill is high. • Stay disciplined so the relationship converts into action.
8|Advantageous
Buyer may say, 'We know you, so this should be easy.' Response: 'I appreciate that trust. I still want to earn this deal properly by aligning tightly to what matters this time.'
Use your history as leverage, but do not get lazy. Convert goodwill into broader access and quicker decisions.
Low risk. Trust is an asset if used well.
Ask: 'Given our past work together, would it help to involve the wider team early and accelerate this?'
Advantageous

• Invest deliberately in trust and relevance. • Show understanding of the customer context through tailored discovery and follow-through. • Create small wins quickly, such as a useful insight, benchmark, or improved proposal framing. • Increase confidence through responsiveness and clarity, not pressure. • Turn neutral history into active preference.
8|Neutral
Buyer may say, 'We do not know you well yet.' Response: 'That is fair. Let me make this easy to evaluate through relevance, proof, and clear follow-through.'
Create trust fast with relevant proof, credible questions, and a no-pressure tone. Let confidence build through clarity.
Risk: Neutral accounts need faster trust-building.
Say: 'Let me keep this simple and useful. I will focus only on what matters to your outcome.'
Neutral

• Reduce perceived risk quickly because the buyer has no prior trust bank with you. • Use case studies, references, demos, and implementation clarity to build credibility. • Keep promises tight and realistic in early conversations. • Ask how they normally evaluate a new partner and what would reassure them. • Act like a safe pair of hands from the first interaction.
8|Never worked
Buyer may say, 'You are new to us.' Response: 'Absolutely, which is why I will keep this practical, transparent, and backed by relevant proof.'
Shorten the trust gap with references, pilot logic, and a low-friction first step. New logos need safety.
Risk: New-account trust gap.
Ask: 'Would a reference conversation or a small first phase help make this easier internally?'
Never worked

• Address the trust issue directly but professionally. • Understand what created the negative perception: service, delivery, commercials, product, or responsiveness. • Do not defend too early. Listen, acknowledge, and reset expectations. • Bring senior sponsorship or a recovery plan if needed. • Rebuild confidence in small steps before pushing for closure.
8|Disadvantageous
Buyer may say, 'We had a poor experience earlier.' Response: 'Thank you for saying that directly. I would like to understand what went wrong so I do not repeat it and can show a better path.'
Acknowledge the history directly and reset the narrative with ownership, not defensiveness. You must earn another chance.
High risk: Past baggage is blocking the deal.
Say: 'I know the earlier experience matters. Let us address that openly and show what will be different this time.'
Disadvantageous
How is our history with this customer ?
